Guides

How many security cameras does a home or small shop need?

There is no magic number. The right amount depends on what you want to protect and how your property is laid out. Still, a few simple questions get you most of the way.

Start with the entry points. Most people begin with the front door and the back door. For a shop, that means the entrance, the counter and any back or loading door.

Add the places things happen. Driveways, side gates, garages and parking areas are common choices at home. In a small office, think about where valuables or cash are kept.

Think about views, not just numbers. One well-placed camera that sees the whole entrance beats two aimed badly. Height, lighting and angle matter.

Plan for night. Check that your cameras can see in the dark and that your lighting does not blind them.

A typical range. Many homes and small businesses end up with about 2 to 8 cameras. Your situation may be different, and that is fine.

Think about storage and phone viewing. You will want to watch live from your phone and look back at recorded clips. Decide how long you want footage kept, and where it is stored.

Respect privacy. Point cameras at your own property and entrances, not at neighbours' windows. If you record employees or customers, check the rules. A lawyer can advise.

Not sure where to start? We plan camera spots during a short visit in Toronto, Ontario and give you an honest quote, with phone viewing set up on install day.
